correctness.rationale: All binary palindrome subsequences contain 0, 1, 2, or 3 marked symbols, and the proof explicitly counts all four disjoint possibilities. Three feasible rectangles for the two-one stratum yield the stated gap formula including zero boundaries; reversing covers the second outer-gap branch. For the asymptotic law, a four-region inequality bounds its quadratic form by 3z^2/16 with equality only at equal gaps, and a uniform O(z) remainder and compactness establish the sharp limit and maximizing rigidity. The nonnegative quadratic certificate was checked symbolically at its actual formula, and package-path verification returned VERIFY_OK for 5,985 exhaustive small gap tuples, 495 direct subsequence-set cases, and 300 larger randomized cases. No finite data are presented as infinite proof.

value.rationale: The explicit infinite four-parameter classification resolves distinct scattered palindrome counts at the first nontrivial three-marker level, including the full two-one Ferrers-region geometry. The sharp 3/16 quadratic extremum and uniqueness of the limiting equispaced configuration are structural consequences not visible from generic DP or palindromic-factor results. This is a natural fixed-composition complexity invariant relevant as a baseline for sparse string reconstruction and higher weights, not an arbitrary finite slice or known-table recomputation.
